question: If I drop a class after September 3, will it still count toward my financial aid enrollment status, and what grade will I get?
gold_answer: Yes, if you drop and receive a WD grade between September 4 and September 17, 2026, the course continues to count toward your enrollment status for financial aid (Federal Pell Grant, FSEOG, Federal Direct Loan and NYS TAP). For example, starting with 12 credits and dropping a 3-credit course on September 17, you remain full-time. The grade is WD: a non-punitive grade for a class dropped via CUNYfirst after the financial aid certification date but before the published withdrawal period. question: What do I need to be considered for the clinical Dental Hygiene program?
gold_answer: Complete the six required prerequisite courses: ENG 1101 (or ENG 1101CO or ENG 1101ML), a Mathematical and Quantitative Reasoning course (3-4 credits), SOC 1101, BIO 2311, BIO 2312, and CHEM 1000 or higher. You are considered for the clinical program during the Fall semester if you are CUNY proficient in writing and math and proficient at or above the 12th grade level in reading, and have completed the 21 or 22 required general education credits with at least a C in biology and chemistry and a minimum combined average of 2.5. Seats are allocated by highest cumulative average, so completing the introductory courses does not guarantee progression; the average GPA for acceptance has been approximately 3.4 or higher. The introductory courses must be completed within four semesters, or you are required to transfer out of the dental hygiene curriculum.

question: I'm a transfer student. How do my general education credits transfer, and what about writing intensive credit?
gold_answer: Under Pathways, courses passed for credit at any CUNY college transfer for credit at any other CUNY college, and Required Common Core, Flexible Common Core and College Option courses transfer in the same category. 'Gateway' courses transfer for major credit at CUNY colleges that offer the major. All Common Core and College Option requirements are waived for students with a prior baccalaureate degree. You can appeal the Pathways category of a transferred course with the Transfer Appeal Form (email transfercreditappeal@citytech.cuny.edu). Writing intensive (WI) courses completed at other CUNY colleges or colleges with articulation agreements count. Required WI courses depend on credits transferred: fewer than 30: 4 for the bachelor's, 2 for the associate; 30-59.9: 3 for the bachelor's, 1 for the associate; 60-89.9: 2 for the bachelor's, none for the associate; 90+: 1 for the bachelor's; prior baccalaureate degree: 0.

question: How do I submit a SAP appeal and what do I need to include?
gold_answer: Submit the appeal through ProVerifier+ at https://cuny.proed.org using your CUNY Login, via the link in your email notification or your CUNYfirst To Do List. question: Should I take an Incomplete or withdraw from my class?
gold_answer: NO ADVICE: state the rules, do not choose for the student. An Incomplete (INC) is for a student who has completed a majority of the coursework but cannot complete the whole course for reasons beyond their control, usually 1-2 assignments or exams that amount to 25% or less of the final grade; if no grade change form is submitted the INC converts to an FIN, a failing grade; students cannot graduate in a semester in which they have an incomplete. A W (Official Withdrawal) is a non-punitive grade when a class is dropped via CUNYfirst during the published withdrawal period.

question: What is the Fresh Start program for students who were dismissed from City Tech?
gold_answer: Students dismissed for failing to meet academic standards may appeal for readmission through Fresh Start if they graduated with an Associate's Degree after their dismissal, and must be readmitted into a Baccalaureate program. question: What happens if I don't pay my tuition bill?
gold_answer: Failure to pay tuition and fees by the due date could result in cancellation of course enrollment, and if the tuition remains unpaid after enrollment a hold is placed on the account that prevents adding or swapping courses. A student who fails to pay tuition or other obligations is denied access to their records and prevented from registering in the future, and the account is turned over to the College's collection agency. The student is responsible for all collection costs, including agency fees, attorney fees and court costs, and non-payment or a default judgment may be reported to credit bureaus. Non-payment and not attending courses are NOT considered an official drop.

question: What is the TAP waiver and who can get one?
gold_answer: A one-time waiver of the good academic standing requirement in the TAP regulations. It is not automatic: it may only be granted in extraordinary or unusual circumstances beyond the student's control and with a reasonable expectation that the student will meet future requirements. To request it, speak to a TAP Counselor in the Financial Aid Office and submit the completed TAP waiver/appeal form.
